mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_CareTeamGating allows the model to produce a Permitted outcome on a RecordLookup or AddNote operation where no ActiveMembership links the caller to the patient. This directly contradicts the care-team ownership invariant (FR-004) and the NoInformationLeakage assertion that denied paths never yield Permitted.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CareTeamGatingViolation { some op: Operation | op.opKind = RecordLookup and op.opOutcome = Permitted and op.opCaller.userRole = Doctor and (no m: ActiveMembership | m.membClinician = op.opCaller and m.membPatient = op.opTargetPatient) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_AdminRestrictedToListAudit allows the model to construct a HospitalAdministrator Operation with opKind = RecordLookup, violating the role-separation invariant. LeastPrivilege will find a counterexample because an admin reaches a clinical endpoint.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AdminReachesClinicialEndpoint { some op: Operation | op.opCaller.userRole = HospitalAdministrator and op.opKind = RecordLookup }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_AuditOperationBijection allows two distinct Operations to share the same AuditEntry, breaking the one-to-one invariant. AuditCompleteness and FR_014_AuditImmutable both assert uniqueness and completeness of the audit-to-operation mapping.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_SharedAuditEntry { some disj op1, op2: Operation | op1.opAuditEntry = op2.opAuditEntry }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_NoteCreatedOnlyForPermittedAddNote allows a ClinicalNote to be linked as opNoteCreated on a Denied or RecordLookup operation. This violates the append-only invariant and the validation-before-mutation invariant: a note would exist without a permitting operation.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_NoteWithoutPermission { some op: Operation | op.opKind = RecordLookup and some op.opNoteCreated }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_AuditNoteRefConstraint allows an AuditEntry with access_type=list_audit or a denied add_note to carry a non-null aeNoteRef, or a permitted add_note to carry no aeNoteRef. FR_013_AuditEntryShape directly checks this structural rule; FR_015_AuditAtomicWithAccess requires the ref to exist on success.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditNoteRefViolation { some ae: AuditEntry | ae.aeAccessType = ListAudit and some ae.aeNoteRef }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_ClinicalRolesCannotAccessListAudit allows a Doctor (or other clinical role) to have an Operation with opKind = ListAudit, breaching the administrator-exclusive audit endpoint invariant. FR_017_AdminOnlyListAudit will immediately find a counterexample.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_ClinicalRoleAccessesListAudit { some op: Operation | op.opCaller.userRole = Doctor and op.opKind = ListAudit }
